title: Resolve priority inversion causing first-token lag in multiplexed workers
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden increases in first-token latency (TTFT) and reduced tokens/sec on multiplexed workers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Problem appears during mixed workloads when short-chat requests interleave with long generation requests. Impact: user-visible TTFT spikes up to 900-1200ms on short requests (normally ~80-120ms) and aggregate tokens/sec drop by 25-40% for affected worker pods. Customers escalated: MarketplaceApp (hosted), FinSight (dedicated), MedData (private/VPC).

Reproduction steps:
1) Deploy model family (gptx-7b-family) with multiplexing enabled and default scheduling.
2) Send 1k short prompt requests (avg 30 tokens) interleaved with 200 long generation requests (avg 600 tokens) across the same worker pool.
3) Observe queue length skew and long-lived requests occupying slots. Short requests incur repeated context switching and prefetch-induced cache evictions, causing TTFT regression.

Investigation notes:
- Root cause appears to be a priority inversion introduced by the scheduler tuning landed in runtime-2.3.0: kernel-selector changed worker affinity heuristics to favor throughput for long sequences; this unintentionally gave long requests preemption over queued short requests when the multiplex queue reached soft capacity.
- A secondary contributing factor: per-tenant KV cache eviction policy recalculated on tail-latency triggers, causing short requests to lose prefix cache entries right when they were scheduled onto a worker.
- Observed in all deployment modes but manifests differently: Hosted shows region-level overload; Dedicated shows tenant-sensitive saturation because reserved pools are shared across multiple product teams; Private customers had manual capacity constraints and slower patch rollouts, worsening customer experience.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix):
- Revert the affinity heuristic change to the previous kernel-selector behavior (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/7192).
- Deploy runtime-2.3.1-hotfix to hosted canary (us-west-2-fastlane) with 5% traffic and monitor TTFT and tokens/sec for 30 minutes.
- Add a conservative per-priority fast-path lane: short requests (<=64 tokens, low token budget) are routed to a bounded fast pool that uses pre-allocated KV sticky shards to avoid eviction on context switches.
- For Dedicated: push ops playbook to apply config patch to reserved pools (ops runbook id: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/fastlane-dedicated).
- For Private: prepare patch notes and backport branch; coordinate with impacted customers for manual upgrade window.

Rollout plan:
- Canary Hosted (us-west-2): runtime-2.3.1-hotfix, 5% traffic -> 30 min metrics burn -> 25% -> full roll.
- Dedicated: staged release to non-critical reserved clusters (2 clusters) -> monitor -> schedule automated roll for remaining clusters during off-peak.
- Private: publish backport and coordinate remediation calls; provide temporary routing config to redirect short requests to a separate fast pool if customers cannot upgrade immediately.

Metrics & dashboards:
- Dashboards to watch: TTFT by model_family, tokens/sec by worker_pool, queue_age_by_priority, kv_cache_hit_by_tenant. Grafana links: grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttft/priority-lane (incident board).
- SLOs to validate: TTFT P95 <= 150ms for short requests, tokens/sec recovered to within 10% of baseline for mixed workloads.

Testing & validation:
- Add synthetic mixed-workload integration test that simulates interleaved short/long streams and asserts TTFT and throughput thresholds.
- Unit tests for scheduler priority preemption and KV cache sticky behavior.
- Performance regression job added to CI with representative model families.

Customer communications:
- Initial triage call held 2026-03-11 with MarketplaceApp and FinSight; shared temporary routing workaround.
- Post-patch announcement template prepared for Hosted and Dedicated customers; Private customers will receive upgrade instructions and change log.

Follow-ups / postmortem actions:
- ENG: formal postmortem and root-cause doc within 5 days.
- Add e2e synthetic monitors that run across deployment modes nightly and alert on TTFT delta >30%.
- Revisit kernel-selector heuristics with perf team and add canary gating to prevent priority inversion regressions in future releases.
- Longer-term: implement token-budget-aware preemption and worker-level QoS counters to prevent long requests from monopolizing worker resources.
